Title: Painter's Colour Palette Sorting Strategy

Intended changes:
- solution repository: add new domain class `Colour` as a record with fields `String name` and `int hex`, implements `Comparable<Colour>` based on `name`, placed at `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Colour.java`.
- template repository: add the same `Colour` class at `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Colour.java` (full implementation, no TODO).
- solution repository: rename method parameter type from `List<Date>` to `List<Colour>` in `BubbleSort.performSort` (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/BubbleSort.java`) and update implementation to use `Colour.compareTo`.
- template repository: rename method parameter type from `List<Date>` to `List<Colour>` in `BubbleSort.performSort` (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/BubbleSort.java`) and adjust TODO comment accordingly.
- solution repository: rename method parameter type from `List<Date>` to `List<Colour>` in `MergeSort.performSort` and all internal helper methods (`mergesort`, `merge`) in `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/MergeSort.java`.
- template repository: rename method parameter type from `List<Date>` to `List<Colour>` in `MergeSort.performSort` and adjust TODO comment in `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/MergeSort.java`.
- solution repository: replace field `private List<Date> dates;` with `private List<Colour> colours;` in `Context.java` (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Context.java`), rename getter/setter to `getColours`/`setColours`, and update `sort()` to use the new field.
- solution repository: update `Policy.java` to use `context.getColours().size()` and adjust messages to refer to colours instead of dates (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Policy.java`).
- solution repository: in `Client.java`, replace all `Date` usages with `Colour`, rename helper method `createRandomDatesList` to `createRandomColoursList`, adjust random generation to produce random `Colour` objects (e.g., random name and hex), and update print statements to refer to colours (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Client.java`).
- template repository: in `Client.java`, make analogous replacements: replace `Date` with `Colour`, rename method to `createRandomColoursList`, adjust TODO comments, and update print statements to refer to colours (file `src/de/tum/cit/aet/sorting/Client.java`).
- test repository: rename all references to `Date` to `Colour` in test source files, including method signatures, variable declarations, and helper methods; adjust imports accordingly.
- test repository: update the structure oracle JSON (e.g., `structure.json`) to expect field `colours` of type `List<Colour>` in class `Context` and method signatures with `List<Colour>`.
- problem statement: rewrite narrative to an imaginative painter's colour palette theme, replace all mentions of dates with colours, rename field and method references in description, and update UML diagram to show `List<Colour>` field and method signatures accordingly.
- problem statement: update UML diagram block to reflect `Context` field `-colours: List<Colour>` and method `+sort()` unchanged, and update `SortStrategy` method signature to `+performSort(List<Colour>)`, and class boxes for `BubbleSort` and `MergeSort` accordingly.

Invariants:
- the number of test cases remains identical; only type names change.
- algorithm class names (BubbleSort, MergeSort, SortStrategy, Context, Policy) stay unchanged.
- build tooling (Maven) and dependency set stay unchanged.
- template repository still compiles but fails the tests (scores 0%).
- solution repository passes all tests after applying changes.
- structural tests continue to check the same public members, now with `Colour` instead of `Date`.

Problem statement:
In the bustling studio of the legendary painter Aurora, the canvas awaits a perfectly ordered palette of colours. To bring harmony to her masterpieces, you must implement sorting algorithms that can arrange a list of colours and select the appropriate algorithm at runtime using the strategy pattern.

### Part 1: Sorting

First, we need to implement two sorting algorithms, in this case `MergeSort` and `BubbleSort`.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][Implement Bubble Sort](<testid>1732</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` in the class `BubbleSort`. Make sure to follow the Bubble Sort algorithm exactly.

2. [task][Implement Merge Sort](<testid>1730</testid>)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` in the class `MergeSort`. Make sure to follow the Merge Sort algorithm exactly.

### Part 2: Strategy Pattern

We want the application to apply different algorithms for sorting a `List` of `Colour` objects.
Use the strategy pattern to select the right sorting algorithm at runtime.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][SortStrategy Interface](<testid>1734</testid>,<testid>1738</testid>)
Create a `SortStrategy` interface and adjust the sorting algorithms so that they implement this interface.

2. [task][Context Class](<testid>1733</testid>,<testid>1737</testid>)
Create and implement a `Context` class following the below class diagram.

3. [task][Context Policy](<testid>1736</testid>,<testid>1729</testid>,<testid>1739</testid>)
Create and implement a `Policy` class following the below class diagram with a simple configuration mechanism:

    1. [task][Select MergeSort](<testid>1731</testid>,<testid>1728</testid>)
    Select `MergeSort` when the palette has more than 10 colours.

    2. [task][Select BubbleSort](<testid>1735</testid>,<testid>1727</testid>)
    Select `BubbleSort` when the palette has less or equal 10 colours.

4. Complete the `Client` class which demonstrates switching between two strategies at runtime.

### Part 3: Optional Challenges

(These are not tested)

1. Create a new class `QuickSort` that implements `SortStrategy` and implement the Quick Sort algorithm.

2. Make the method `performSort(List<Colour>)` generic, so that other objects can also be sorted by the same method.
   **Hint:** Have a look at Java Generics and the interface `Comparable`.

3. Think about a useful decision in `Policy` when to use the new `QuickSort` algorithm.
